answer_summary: X = I (iodine only). A 2.5 V electron carries e*V = 2.5 eV = 241.1811 kJ/mol (using printed constants e = 1.602e-19 C, N_A = 6.022e23 mol^-1). This energy reaches only BDE(C-I) = 228 kJ/mol among the table values (467, 346, 290, 228), so iodine is the unique possible halogen in the reagent for the 2.5 V retro-Bergman synthesis of C18.
assumptions: Problem inputs (printed data): BDE table {C-F: 467, C-Cl: 346, C-Br: 290, C-I: 228} kJ/mol; applied voltage 2.5 V; constants e = 1.602e-19 C and N_A = 6.022e23 mol^-1 from the official constant sheet G1-3.

Trusted general physical law: a voltage-driven dissociative cleavage of a C-X bond by one accelerated electron requires the electron kinetic energy (per mole) to be at least the C-X bond dissociation energy. Hence Possible X iff BDE(C-X) <= e*V*N_A.
